text.aria-label: Title text 'Figure 2: For wind power, each weather product's error minus the ENS mean's error, by lead day'
text.tspan: Figure 2: For wind power, each weather product's error minus the ENS
mean's error, by lead day

text.aria-label: Subtitle text 'Each row is an XGBoost model given one product's weather for the three wind farms. Dot: the product's error minus the ENS mean's at the same lead day, in percentage points of capacity; negative means the product forecasts better. Zero is the ENS mean. Where a 95% interval includes zero, the product and the ENS mean are not distinguished. Dot: estimate. Line: 95% interval from resampling whole months and a fitting seed. Dashed line: an interval from fewer than 12 months, which a month-block bootstrap tends to draw too narrow. AIFS Single, AIFS ENS mean, and WeatherNext 3 have two marks. Filled dot: against an ENS mean refitted on the same 16, 11, or 7 months. Hollow diamond: against the leaderboard's 21-month ENS mean, on the same hours. For wind, WeatherNext 3's filled dot is against the ENS mean-vector reference. Each row is scored on the hours its product and its reference share. Day 0 is not a lead a live service could use. Lead mismatch: at days 0 to 7, UKV, ICON-D2, ICON-EU, ICON global, GFS (Open-Meteo), IFS 0.25°, ARPEGE, AROME, and both HARMONIE-AROME products read the freshest run at least N days old, a shorter lead than ENS's on most hours, and native GFS does at day 0. That favours those products, so a higher error than ENS is conservative for them, and a lower error is not evidence of skill at equal lead. Every error is a fraction of the generator's own capacity, taken as its 99th percentile of metered output. Caveat (hollow circle in place of the filled dot): WeatherNext 3's day-10 weather scored no better than shuffled weather in this fit (19.00% against 18.80% and 18.94%); the cause is not established and this is not evidence that WeatherNext 3 loses skill. All rows are exploratory.'
text.tspan: Each row is an XGBoost model given one product's weather for the three wind farms. Dot: the product's error minus
the ENS mean's at the same lead day, in percentage points of capacity; negative means the product forecasts better.
Zero is the ENS mean. Where a 95% interval includes zero, the product and the ENS mean are not distinguished.
Dot: estimate. Line: 95% interval from resampling whole months and a fitting seed.
Dashed line: an interval from fewer than 12 months, which a month-block bootstrap tends to draw too narrow.
AIFS Single, AIFS ENS mean, and WeatherNext 3 have two marks. Filled dot: against an ENS mean refitted on the same
16, 11, or 7 months. Hollow diamond: against the leaderboard's 21-month ENS mean, on the same hours. For wind,
WeatherNext 3's filled dot is against the ENS mean-vector reference.
Each row is scored on the hours its product and its reference share. Day 0 is not a lead a live service could use.
Lead mismatch: at days 0 to 7, UKV, ICON-D2, ICON-EU, ICON global, GFS (Open-Meteo), IFS 0.25°, ARPEGE, AROME, and
both HARMONIE-AROME products read the freshest run at least N days old, a shorter lead than ENS's on most hours,
and native GFS does at day 0. That favours those products, so a higher error than ENS is conservative for them, and
a lower error is not evidence of skill at equal lead.
Every error is a fraction of the generator's own capacity, taken as its 99th percentile of metered output.
Caveat (hollow circle in place of the filled dot): WeatherNext 3's day-10 weather scored no better than shuffled
weather in this fit (19.00% against 18.80% and 18.94%); the cause is not established and this is not evidence that
WeatherNext 3 loses skill.
All rows are exploratory.
